conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask:

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure, to be honest. He goes to college, but I don't know if that counts as "approved education" or not. What exactly does that mean?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a helpful question! College typically does count as approved education. Let me clarify what "approved education or training" means for Child Benefit purposes:

For young people aged 16-19, approved education generally includes:
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or equivalent qualifications at school or college)
- Courses up to and including Level 3 (England), Advanced Higher (Scotland), or Level 3 (Wales and Northern Ireland)
- The course must be more than 12 hours a week of supervised study or course-related work experience

So to help determine if Alex's college course qualifies, can you tell me:

Is Alex studying full-time at college (more than 12 hours per week of supervised study)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. Well, he does go to college regularly during the week, so yes, it's definitely more than 12 hours a week. He's there most days.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that. It sounds like Alex is in full-time education which is positive for your claim.

Now I need to ask about your circumstances: Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Now, a very important question for eligibility:

Are you currently responsible for Alex? This usually means either:
- You live with him, OR
- You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him - for example on food, clothes or pocket money

Do either of these apply to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? (Only one person can get Child Benefit for the same child)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete my assessment:

Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work that much - he's focused on his studies at college. And he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why you qualify:
- Alex is 17 years old (under 20)
- He's in full-time approved education at college (more than 12 hours per week)
- He lives with you in the UK
- You're responsible for him
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- He's not working 24+ hours per week or receiving his own benefits

**Important note:** Please be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit and receive the payments, but you may need to pay some or all of it back through your tax return.

Child Benefit will continue for Alex as long as he remains in approved education or training, until he turns 20. If his circumstances change (such as leaving education or starting work for 24+ hours per week), you'll need to inform HMRC.

Would you like any information about how to make your claim?
